e-532.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040080/assets/299365e1a9d092be299966bd49858b2245b86dad846e67ae2873b30ea0bd6ac9.png)

Sketch the slope field of the differential equation $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} = 4x+2$ at the points indicated in the diagram above.
e-532.worked_solution:
We have to sketch the slope fields at the points $(-1,-2), (0,-2),$ and $(0,1).$

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-2)}=4(-1)+2=-2 \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(0,-2)}=4(0)+2=2 \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(0,1)}=4(0)+2=2\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040080/assets/617673605e9f13423851496fcfc79d7d60bda5c0569438943ca303c812b68885.png)
